boards.title: Your First Weekend at Temple University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe sequence that starts on Main Campus, builds in campus resources and art, then adds nearby North Philadelphia and a historic-city stop.

cards.title: Start at the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • Main Campus
cards.notes: Use the Bell Tower as a clear first meeting point, then orient yourself with the nearby pedestrian walks before choosing the next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable Main Campus landmark for beginning the weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple’s official Main Campus map labels the Bell Tower on Main Campus.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus landmark; use normal campus-access practices.

cards.title: Pause in Founder’s Garden
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Main Campus
cards.notes: Walk through the pocket garden and look for Russell Conwell’s bust and grave; it gives a concrete introduction to Temple’s early history.
cards.short_summary: A small campus garden tied directly to Temple’s founder.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple states that Russell and Sarah Conwell were reburied in Founder’s Garden, behind a bust of Conwell.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus garden; follow posted campus rules.

cards.title: Take a game-room break
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Howard Gittis Student Center
cards.notes: Head to the HGSC Game Room for pool, ping-pong, video games, or board games, and use the pause to get acquainted with the student center.
cards.short_summary: A casual indoor activity inside Temple’s main student center.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Student Affairs lists pool, ping-pong, video games, and board games at the HGSC Game Room.
cards.source_title: Howard Gittis Student Center | Student Center Operations
cards.access_notes: Check current student-center hours and any participation requirements before going.

cards.title: Make Charles Library your reset point
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • 1900 N. 13th Street
cards.notes: Walk the reading areas and flexible spaces, then choose one practical next-week task to handle while you are already on Main Campus.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s main library offers study areas and collaborative spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries describes Charles Library as Main Campus’s library, with reading areas, student study spaces, and a 24/7 area.
cards.access_notes: Verify current hours. The 24/7 space requires a valid OwlCard when the main library is closed.

cards.title: See the BookBot in Charles
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Charles Library
cards.notes: Find the visible Automated Storage and Retrieval System and request a title later if you need it; the BookBot is a useful landmark for remembering the library layout.
cards.short_summary: A named automated storage system holding library materials.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple Libraries identifies Charles Library’s Automated Storage and Retrieval System as BookBot and says items can be pulled for pickup.
cards.access_notes: BookBot retrieval follows the library’s current service hours and borrowing rules.

cards.entity_name: Independence Blue Cross Student Recreation Center
cards.title: Move at the IBC Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • 1701 N. 15th Street
cards.notes: If you have recreation access, choose a short workout or indoor-track walk, then leave time to shower and continue the day without rushing.
cards.short_summary: Temple’s primary general-fitness facility with an indoor track.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple identifies the IBC Student Recreation Center as its primary general-fitness facility and lists its indoor track and fitness equipment.
cards.source_title: Independence Blue Cross Student Recreation Center | Temple University
cards.access_notes: Access is for Temple students, staff, and faculty who have paid the recreation fee; patrons must be at least 18.

cards.title: Visit Temple Contemporary
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday • Tyler School of Art and Architecture
cards.notes: Enter Tyler through the Norris Street entrance and spend time with the current exhibition; check the gallery calendar before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: A public contemporary-art gallery in Temple’s Tyler School.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says Temple Contemporary is a 3,400-square-foot gallery that is free and open to all, Tuesday through Saturday.
cards.source_title: Temple Contemporary Gallery | Tyler School of Art and Architecture
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Tuesday–Saturday, 11 a.m.–6 p.m.; enter Tyler via Norris Street between 12th and 13th Streets.

cards.title: Check what’s on at TPAC
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • 1837 N. Broad Street
cards.notes: Stop outside the former Baptist Temple, then check the event calendar for an appropriate public concert, film screening, lecture, or performance.
cards.short_summary: A historic Temple venue for recurring music, film, and lecture programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Temple says TPAC hosts large Boyer ensembles as well as Jazz Café, film screenings, guest lectures, and classes.
cards.source_title: Temple Performing Arts Center | Boyer College of Music and Dance
cards.access_notes: Programs and ticketing vary; confirm the event’s date, age guidance, and admission details before attending.

cards.title: Explore the Wagner’s specimen hall
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • 1700 W. Montgomery Avenue
cards.notes: Plan this near-campus museum for a first-Saturday opening, then follow a themed scavenger hunt or sketch from the natural-history collection.
cards.short_summary: A Victorian natural-history museum with more than 100,000 specimens.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wagner states that its museum is free to visit and its upstairs exhibit hall holds more than 100,000 natural specimens.
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday and on the first Saturday of select months; verify the current calendar and register if required.

cards.title: Finish with the Liberty Bell
cards.subtitle: Sunday daytime • Independence National Historical Park
cards.notes: Build in security time and use the exhibits as context before viewing the Bell; entry is first come, first served, so choose an unhurried arrival.
cards.short_summary: A free National Park Service stop centered on the Liberty Bell.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the Liberty Bell Center is free, needs no ticket, and admits visitors first come, first served.
cards.source_title: Independence National Historical Park Field Trip FAQs | National Park Service
cards.access_notes: No ticket is required, but visitors pass through security and waiting time varies; check current park conditions before travel.
